To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel dehalgenase was purified, cloned and characterized from Bacillus sp GZT, which could efficiently degrade 2,4.6-tribromphenol in aqueous solutions.
a novel dehalgenase was isolated from a TBP degrader, which could be used for bioremediation of TBP-contaminated environment.
we have isolated, purified and characterized a novel TBP-degrading dehalogenase, which can efficiently degrade TBP and may be a potential tool for TBP remediation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the purification of the novel dehalogenases and the cloning and characterization of the gene encoding the dehalogenases.
the identification of a novel TBP dehalgenase, which could be used as a potential biocatalyst in bioremediation.
the identification of a novel degradative pathway of TBP, which will provide new insights into its environmental fate and the potential bioremediation strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TBP dehaloenase was a novel enzyme that could be applied in bioremediation of TBP pollution in the future.
the novel dehalogenases could play a key role in the degradation of TBP, and the enzyme may provide a new strategy for bioremediation and biotransformation of halogenated pollutants.
this study provides a novel dehaloenase from Bacillus for TBP bioremediation, and the gene encoding this dehaloenase can be cloned and expressed in E. coli for further research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we successfully isolated an efficient TBP degrader strain from the contaminated soil and purified a novel dehalogenic enzyme from it.

the TBP degradation pathway of Bacillus sp. GZT might be a two-step reaction: firstly, the dehalgenase catalyzed TBP debromination to 2,6-dibromophenol; and then the dibromophenol was further degraded by other enzymes.
the TBP dehalo-genase could not only improve the degradation rate of TBP, but also be a new target for further research on the degradation mechanism of TBP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the enzyme could be a good candidate for the biodegradation and detoxification of TBP in water.
we have successfully purified a dehalogenase that is capable of degrading 2,4-tribromophenal (TBP).
we successfully purified, cloned and expressed the novel dehalogenases from GZT, which can efficiently catalyze the debromination of 2, 4, 6-TBP.
